Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from Village of Nakusp, about 67 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 23, Hwy 31.
Park: 50.42295, -117.14641, pull off on Hwy 31 (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 160 m SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 40 m, about 7 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: elk, Sept, Oct (season rows). Glass the edge of the 2017 burn (right here: grass and shrubs) at first and last light; in September listen for bugling bulls. Keep the wind in your face (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-30, Region 4. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R4D-elk-drive-0001.popWhy: Popular (more hunters): MU 4-30: about 238 hunter days a year for elk (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.18 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: close to pavement, a town or a rec site. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.2 km and about 40 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R4D-grouse-walk-0003.name: By Cascade Creek
R4D-grouse-walk-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R4D-grouse-walk-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed paved road

evidence.t: Trail: Cascade Cr Trail, 4.8 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
4 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
16 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

flags.t: Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 4 table (pages 39 and 40), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis). Pages 36 to 41 print no LEH list.

plan: Drive: from Village of Nakusp, about 59 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.37174, -117.20169, pull off on an unnamed paved road. Map links below.
Walk 3.9 km to the start. Walk: the Cascade Cr Trail stretch, 4.8 km one way. About 96 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-30, Region 4. No baiting in Region 4. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
